context: Application in dynamic algorithm also seems to be a promising approach. Frandsen and Sankowski [13] showed an algorithm, that dynamically preserves Frobenius normal form in O(kn2 ) time. Our algorithms use fast Hankel matrix-vector multiplication. The algorithm behind fast Hankel matrix-vector multiplication is based on Discrete Fourier Transform √ (DFT). Reif and Tate [20] presented an O( n) time per request algorithm for DFT. Can we use those approaches to obtain a faster dynamic algorithm? Finally, it remains open how to apply the Frobenius normal form in the weighted directed graphs with small, integer weights {−M, . . . , M }. Cygan et al. [9] took degree M polynomials e nω ) time.
